questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always had a profound interest for Australia. I love the nature, the weather, the animal life, and just the friendliness of the Australian people. Therefore, it was a no-brainer for me likewise, studying at a good univeristy was an uncanny opportunity like no other.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you are ever in doubt about one thing in your life, please dont let it be whether to go on an exhcange program or not! Just do it! You will learn so much about yourself and grow to be a better you. You will have the hardest and the best time of your life and I promise it is worth every sad and happy tear, as you leave to go on exchange full of hope and maybe a little afraid, to crying over the assignments or due to homesickness, to having a laugh at dinner with your new friends, to finally crying in the airport (Yes, you will cry) when you eventually have to leave because you leave a piece of yourself in that place. I promise that is how much an exchange program is gonna mean to you. You will be enriched for life and when you grow old it will be hell of a story to say you lived in another city in your 20s. Not many people have that privilege to call two cities home, so use it!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The student advisors guided you all the way. You really should not stress about all the formalities such as visa and all that. Though the advisors may be a bit slow to respond to you since they have a lot of student to handle. I had one obligatory intro day, which was essentially no new info since everything had been said in emails already
University of Sydneys homepage is also a million times better than KUs so its easy to find information there

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didnt receive any assistance though you can book a free busride from the airport to your accomodation which was something I found out too late unfortunetaly. Use it the ride from the airport is really expensive!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think it was good. I didnt neccesarily need anything since all had already been sent in emails

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Your advisor will send you an email to let you know your options. But it is usually very late that they send it to you so I would say go out and look on your own. The two most popular for USYD is Iglu, Scape.
But dont worry there will still be room for you! I loved my time at IGlu, it is soooooooo expensive but really the best expericence ever, youre gonna meet so many new friends with all the activities they hold, free breakfast, and study rooms and gaming rooms where you can meet with your new freidsn. I would highly reccomend Iglu!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very very expensive to rent in Sydney, try to be early and find a shared apartment with others if you have the opportunity or find on Airbnb if possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing is really nice its just way too expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They sent you a detailed email how to, what they call ‘enrol’ into your course. Really try to think of the units you want to study cause I found it quite a hassle to change my units. You had to fill out a pdf form, send it to the advisor, and then you would have to wait for them to change it for you, which can take some time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to enrol in the coursework. Fill out some personal details, say I want these four units (you have to suggest 8 to them and they will say yes or no) and then you jsut pick your units.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write to your advisor, they were kinda like your personal assistant really.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all 4 that I wanted, I had no problem. I was a masters student so I think that was easier for me than bachelors

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Think about the units that you want to study and pick something that is related to your field of study. If they deem you not fit for this unit they will not allow you to take it. There are a lot of options so dont worry. But it is quite a hassle to change your units just so you know. For me they were quite lenient so that was nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can definelty feel that it is a top univeristy much better than KU in my opinion they content is more modern.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of course was easier than or almost the same as KU I would say. It is more practical and KU is more theoretical is what I found.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Lectures are essentially the same, but be aware they start at the time advised not liek at KU where it is 15 min past. And they only hold a 5 minute break in the middle of the lecture not 15, which was really hard I thougjt.
The tutorials are almost like KU too, although some of them are shorter and more compressed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BUSS6002 Data Science in Business
QBUS6810: Machine Learning for Business
QBUS6840: Predictive Analytics
QBUS6860: Visual Data Analytics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
QBUS6860: Visual Data Analytics is a really easy unit. If you make an okay effort on the assignments you dont have to attend the final exam!
QBUS6810: Machine Learning for Business was one of the most interestting units I have ever taken would highly reccomend if youre into Data Science and what to work with it, it will prepare you for that.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When I moved into my student apartment I had to buy a matress, cups, utensils and so on.. which can run up in price really quickly.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transportation is really cheap. You can get a student Opal card so you will save 50% on all your trips compared to normal price.
It is actually really cheap to eat out in Sydney, especially compared to Copenhagen.
Groceries are more expensive here
Most museums are free

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didnt join a club but I think there is more than 200 clubs so you have plenty of choice!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports (they even have their own football pitch and swimming pool) and chocolate club, book club everything you can think of there is a club for it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you get the chance to vacation around in Australia please do it. Australia is so much more than Sydney even though it is a nice city is gets pretty boring fast. It is also relatively cheap to fly around Australia.
You can go to a wilflife sanctuary if you want to pet a kangaroo (highly recommend) or just go to a nice nature walk around Bondi/Manly.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If the weather is nice take the ferry to Manly and eat at Yochi and the fish and chips shop. Otherwise just look at tiktok/pinterest

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Sydney is actually a really interesting city. It is a mix between Europe and Asia. The transition will really not be that hard as Australians are really close culturally with British/US and Western Europeans, but you can also go to Chinatown and you will literally not feel like you are in Sydney anymore bu like Hong Kong. Very multicultural, really brings out the best of the city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Expect your classes to be 95% international Chinese students and Indian students. If you want to socialise you should dare to go up and talk to them they will not come and talk to you. Also a good idea is to take a unit which contains group work that will force you to socialize which is really good, it worked for me at least.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
They drive on the left hand side. I was so close to getting run over a million times until I learned to look the right way when crossing :-D A lot of the Chinese students are quite hard to understand sometimes and also it can be challenging understanding cultural differences but that is also part of the fun, and you will learn a lot about Chinese culture haha (but I mean it i a good way, it actually interesting)
Each time you walk into a clothing store they are almost harrasing you and asking what they can help me so annoying.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Australians are so friendly and will talk to everyone. Honestly just go to a bar or even at the stoplight.
The food culture in Sydney is propably the best in the world. They have the best European and Asian food omg, that is the one thing I am gonna miss the most about Sydney!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be aware of the English requirements maybe you have to take an English test!
2) Save up. Sydney is expensive
3) Have as much fun as possible, sometimes just say screw uni and go do what you want. Dont take school too seriously when youre on exchange

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Having to challenge myself each and every single day and getting out of my comfort zone, by socializing always trying to make frineds and cant let a rejection set you astray. I became way more confident in both myself and my English skills.
Having finished all my units was really rewarding even though I didnt get perfect scores I did my best at one of the best univesities in the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to sozialise. It is hard to travel to a new country on your own without knowing noone there or have maybe never even been there before so you also have to get used to the culture. It is propably the hardest part of going on exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
